sections.heading: C — Parking and insurance
sections.markdown:
## C — Parking and insurance

FACT_ID: sec08-F01 | anchor: A01
Before turning right across a cyclist in the lane, confirm the rider has yielded or passed, since bikes should pass left but often do not. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0054]

FACT_ID: sec08-F02 | anchor: A01
Bicycles are hard to see and need no daytime lights, unlike motorcycles. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0054]

FACT_ID: sec08-F03 | anchor: A01
Many young cyclists never trained or tested, so give children on bikes extra caution. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0054]

FACT_ID: sec08-F04 | anchor: A01
Share the road respectfully without honking, shouting or swerving at cyclists, which can startle them into a crash. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0054]

FACT_ID: sec08-F05 | anchor: A01
Night bicycles need a front white light visible at least five hundred feet ahead. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0054]

FACT_ID: sec08-F06 | anchor: A01
Rear red lights visible five hundred feet back are optional extras beside the mandatory rear reflectors. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0054]

FACT_ID: sec08-F07 | anchor: A01
Night bicycles need reflective sidewalls or spoke reflectors on both wheels, with spoke units near the rim and visible both sides in the stated colors. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0054]

FACT_ID: sec08-F08 | anchor: A01
Bicycle brakes must be strong enough to skid the wheels on dry, level, clean pavement. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0054]

FACT_ID: sec08-F09 | anchor: A01
A fluorescent orange flag six feet above the road is encouraged for visibility from behind. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0054]

FACT_ID: sec08-F10 | anchor: A01
Treat bicycles as vehicles, watching entries, bikeways, sidewalks, turns and children darting between parked cars. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0054]

FACT_ID: sec08-F11 | anchor: A01
Park clear of travel lanes and visible to approaching traffic from both directions. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0054]

FACT_ID: sec08-F12 | anchor: A01
Use marked areas, set the brake, and leave a manual in gear or an automatic in park. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0054]

FACT_ID: sec08-F13 | anchor: A01
Check traffic before opening doors, exit curbside when possible, and close doors promptly. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0054]

FACT_ID: sec08-F14 | anchor: A01
Never leave keys inside; lock up whenever leaving the vehicle. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0054]

FACT_ID: sec08-F15 | anchor: A01
On roadways park as far from traffic as possible, hugging the curb or the shoulder edge. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0054]

FACT_ID: sec08-F16 | anchor: A01
The vehicle must sit within eighteen inches of the curb or shoulder edge. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0054]

FACT_ID: sec08-F17 | anchor: A02
Roadway or shoulder parking at night needs front and rear lights visible five hundred feet, with headlights dimmed. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0055]

FACT_ID: sec08-F18 | anchor: A02
Signal when leaving a space, scanning both ways and double-checking for vehicles, bikes and pedestrians when backing out. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0055]

FACT_ID: sec08-F19 | anchor: A02
Parallel parking starts with a signal, aligning beside the lead car at least two feet out with rear bumpers even. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0055]

FACT_ID: sec08-F20 | anchor: A02
Reverse to the lead car front door, cut sharply right to a forty-five-degree angle, then swing left while backing in and straighten forward. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0055]

FACT_ID: sec08-F21 | anchor: A02
Hill parking turns the wheels sharply roadside so a rollaway leaves traffic; downhill aims at the curb, uphill away, and curb-free uphill aims away from the street. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0055]

FACT_ID: sec08-F22 | anchor: A03
Curb colors limit stopping: white for passenger pickup and drop-off, yellow for attended loading, red for no stopping, standing or parking. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0056]

FACT_ID: sec08-F23 | anchor: A03
Never park inside an intersection or within twenty feet of its crosswalk or sidewalk. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0056]

FACT_ID: sec08-F24 | anchor: A03
Never park where construction blockage results, or within thirty feet of a signal, stop sign or yield sign. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0056]

FACT_ID: sec08-F25 | anchor: A03
Keep fifteen feet from fire hydrants and fifty feet from railroad crossings. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0056]

FACT_ID: sec08-F26 | anchor: A03
Stay within eighteen inches of the curb and clear of fire-station driveways by twenty feet same-side or seventy-five across. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0056]

FACT_ID: sec08-F27 | anchor: A03
Never block driveways, alleys, private roads or curb cuts for sidewalk access. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0056]

FACT_ID: sec08-F28 | anchor: A03
Never park on a bridge, elevated structure, tunnel or underpass. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0056]

FACT_ID: sec08-F29 | anchor: A03
Never park on the wrong side, alongside another parked vehicle, or on railroad tracks. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0056]

FACT_ID: sec08-F30 | anchor: A03
Never park where a sign forbids it or in a marked accessible space without a permit; violations draw fines. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0056]

FACT_ID: sec08-F31 | anchor: A04
Liability insurance is mandatory except for motorcycles, at twenty-five thousand per person, fifty thousand per accident, and ten thousand for the property of others. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0057]

FACT_ID: sec08-F32 | anchor: A04
Stopped or crashed motorists show insurance evidence to officers with license and registration, and evidence rides in the vehicle always. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0057]

FACT_ID: sec08-F33 | anchor: A04
Uninsured driving is a misdemeanor: a first offense draws at least two hundred fifty up to five hundred dollars, up to ten days in jail, or both, plus five record points. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0057]

FACT_ID: sec08-F34 | anchor: A04
Repeat uninsured driving draws at least three hundred fifty dollars or up to ten days in jail, with plate and registration suspension for ninety days, or one hundred eighty for a third or later offense. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0057]

FACT_ID: sec08-F35 | anchor: A04
Crash responsibility without payment within sixty days suspends license and registration automatically until payment or six years pass, plus fresh insurance evidence. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0057]

FACT_ID: sec08-F36 | anchor: A04
Owners of more than twenty-five Montana-registered vehicles may qualify as self-insurers. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0057]

FACT_ID: sec08-F37 | anchor: A04
Non-residents face the same responsibility law on adequate in-state policies, losing Montana driving privileges for noncompliance with notice to their home state. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0057]

FACT_ID: sec08-F38 | anchor: A04
The insurance verification system matches registration and insurer data so officers, courts, licensing offices and the public can confirm coverage in real time. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0057]

Misconceptions: Dimmed lights still show on a night-parked car; an accessible space needs a permit even for a moment.
Mnemonics: Authored cue: curb close, wheels curbed on hills, papers aboard, coverage current.
Glossary: Shoulder; parallel parking; curb marking; liability insurance; self-insurer; verification system.
Dynamic facts: Posted parking limits, fine amounts and insurance minimums change by law; obey the displayed control and current statute.
